keyVerseText: But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come. have: or, end, or, finish
rootMeaning: The Greek verb τελέω (teléō) derives from the noun τέλος (télos), which signifies an end, goal, or purpose. This root conveys the idea of reaching a limit or conclusion, whether literal or figurative, such as the completion of an action or the fulfillment of a purpose. The word’s etymology emphasizes not just finishing but accomplishing what was intended, highlighting the notion of bringing something to its intended consummation or paying what is due.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, τελέω appears 26 times and is commonly translated with terms such as 'had finished,' 'had made an end,' and 'be accomplished.' This range of translations reveals its consistent use to express the completion or fulfillment of actions, events, or obligations. It can denote physical completion, like finishing a journey, or the execution of a task or promise, reflecting its broad but focused semantic range. The word also carries a sense of paying or discharging a debt, showing its practical application in various contexts.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding τελέω enriches our grasp of biblical fulfillment and divine purpose. The word’s emphasis on completing and accomplishing aligns with the Christian understanding of God’s sovereign plan being perfectly carried out in Christ. Jesus’ mission on earth, including his suffering, death, and resurrection, can be seen as the ultimate τελέω—bringing God’s redemptive work to its intended completion. This word reminds believers that God's promises and commands are not left unfinished but are fully executed according to His perfect will, encouraging faith in the certainty and reliability of divine action.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 10:23 uses τελέω to convey the idea that the apostles will not have completed their mission of preaching throughout the cities of Israel before the coming of the Son of Man. The word highlights the ongoing nature of their task and the divine timing involved. It underscores that their work has a divinely appointed end point, reinforcing the certainty that God’s redemptive plan will be fulfilled in due time. This adds a layer of assurance that the mission is purposeful and will reach its intended conclusion under God’s sovereign control.
